final_claim.narrative: Candidate change point t=24140 with 5000-unit half-windows. Group members 25 and 1763 both show complete (Jaccard=0) replacement of their contact sets across the change point, and critically they switch onto a shared new cohort (66,526,702,850,1566) after having shared an old cohort (65,163,442,978,987,1587). Confounder controls rule out the alternatives: total event volume is flat across all six 5k bins (step_01) and per-node event counts and distinct-partner counts are essentially unchanged before vs. after (steps 03-04), so this is partner-identity substitution rather than a burst, a popularity surge, or a drop in activity. The graph-wide repeat ratio of 0.156 (step_02) shows the network is largely non-repeating, but background churn alone would not synchronize separate members onto one common replacement set at a single instant.
